newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Communists say Yeltsin's NATO deal is a mistake.
newsitem.headline: Communists say Yeltsin's NATO deal is a mistake.

text.p: The head of Russia's Communist Party said on Friday a promised deal between Russia and NATO was a "historic mistake", but a member of the government party said President Boris Yeltsin was trying to force NATO concessions.

Communist leader Gennady Zyuganov, whose party dominates the lower house of parliament, told Interfax news agency that Yeltsin, who flew back to Russia on Friday after talks on NATO in Germany with Chancellor Helmut Kohl, had "given up everything he possibly could".
"Now only national security is left, and he has decided to make a deal even on that," Zyuganov said.

"Apparently, NATO made an ultimatum to the Russian president, and none of his friends -- Bill (Clinton), Kohl -- took Russia's interest into account," he added, calling Yeltsin's announcement an "historic mistake."

Alexander Shokhin, the deputy chairman of the State Duma (lower house), told Interfax that Yeltsin's announcement that he was ready to sign a deal with NATO on May 27 was an attempt to speed things up.
"His declaration is a means to apply pressure on NATO's partners," Shokhin told Interfax news agency. "Yeltsin apparently wants to advance that 20 percent of questions which are still undecided."
NATO is expected to invite Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic to join the alliance at its next summit in July, despite strong opposition from Russia.

Moscow is seeking a special charter outlining its relationship with the alliance and Yeltsin, speaking after his talks with Kohl, said on Thursday that Russia would sign the NATO deal on May 27th in Paris.
Russian deputies said the main undecided issues included the relationship between NATO's military structure and its new members.
"There are still serious problems on the packet of military questions," Vladimir Lukin, head of the Duma's international relations committee, told Interfax.
The United States has already reacted coolly to Yeltsin's announcement that a deal would be signed next month.
U.S. officials said a NATO-Russia agreement was anything but concluded and expressed puzzlement that Russian leaders had acted as if a signing ceremony was definite.
"The Russians are, for some reason I don't entirely understand, talking about this as if it were agreed," a senior U.S. official told Reuters.
Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, who has done much of the negotiation on NATO, had been expected to meet the Foreign Minister of NATO member Portugal on Friday.
But a spokesman said Primakov had been taken ill with gallstone problems. Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Avdeyev took his place at the meeting with Jaime Gama in Moscow.
